class: An action taken on a guess instead of evidence: sign-in to an account not known to be usable
symptom: Waystar (Workday), 1 October: the agent created the account, Workday left the form without signing in, and the agent signed in at once; Workday refused (the email was not verified), the refusal counted towards a lock, and nothing recorded that the account now existed.
site: Workday and any ATS that verifies new accounts by email
root_cause: After an unconfirmed creation the 28 September rule signed in once, before looking for the verification email the 30 September rule allows the agent to open; and remember_account ran only after a confirmed creation, so the account was not on record.
why_tests_missed: The test asserted the sign-in happened (the old rule) and used a page where it succeeded or was refused; none checked that a verification email was looked for first, or that the account was recorded.
fix: On an unconfirmed creation the account is recorded at once ('created, not yet verified'). Then the agent gets itself in without asking (owner, 1 October): it opens the verification link from the applying address's Gmail if one came within 60s; with none it signs in once (the site may not verify); if that is refused it looks for a late verification email once more, opens it and signs in again. Only if all of that fails is the owner needed. Gmail is opened for the applying address (authuser), not /mail/u/0/: the agent's browser holds two Google accounts, and the verification email was looked for in the wrong inbox. A refused sign-in to an account on record also looks for the verification email (last 3 days) before any password reset: an unverified account is refused in the same words as a wrong password. Opening the verification link lifts the earlier refusals (login_guard.account_verified), and a sign-in held by refusals for an account on record first opens the verification email, then signs in.
prevention: Before an action that can cost an attempt (a sign-in, a submit), require positive evidence that it can succeed; record what is known (an account exists) the moment it is known.
